pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Inclusions & SEND
pageCache.text:
Inclusion and SEND
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we are committed to being an inclusive school where every child is valued, supported and encouraged to achieve their best.We recognise that children learn and develop in different ways and that some children may need additional support at different points in their school journey. Our staff work closely with children, families and, where appropriate, external professionals to understand individual needs and ensure children can access learning and participate fully in school life.We place particular importance on relationships, wellbeing and belonging. By knowing our children well and working in partnership with families, we aim to provide the right support at the right time while maintaining high expectations for every child.
Our Inclusion Team
SEND & Inclusion (ID 1321)

Our inclusion team works alongside teachers, support staff, families and external professionals to coordinate support for children across the school.
If you have concerns about your child's learning, development or additional needs, we encourage you to speak initially with your child's class teacher. Our SENCO can also be contacted through the school office at: info.bps@ilpartnership.org
Our Approach to SEND
Our approach begins with high-quality, inclusive teaching for all children. Where a child needs additional support, we work with families to identify their needs, consider appropriate strategies and provision, and review the impact of the support provided.
We make reasonable adjustments where appropriate and work with specialist services and other professionals when additional advice or expertise is required.
Full details of how we identify and support children with SEND can be found in our SEND Information Report and SEND Policy below.
SEND Information Report - 2026-2027
Thrive at Blackfield
Blackfield is a Thrive school. Thrive is a whole-school approach that helps us support children's social and emotional development and recognises the importance of strong, positive relationships in helping children to learn and flourish.
Our staff use Thrive-informed approaches throughout school to help children understand and regulate their emotions, develop resilience and build positive relationships. Some children may also benefit from more targeted support from trained Thrive practitioners when appropriate.
At the heart of our approach is the understanding that behaviour is communication. We seek to understand what children may be communicating through their behaviour and support them to develop the skills they need to manage emotions and engage successfully with school life.
Working with Families
We believe that the best outcomes for children are achieved when school and families work together.
Alongside individual conversations and support, we provide opportunities for parents and carers to develop their understanding of children's learning, behaviour and emotional wellbeing. This includes parent workshops and information sessions on areas such as anxiety, emotional regulation and supporting children's needs.
Where appropriate, our inclusion and family support staff can also help families access advice, resources and support from other services.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - English - Reading
pageCache.text:
English - Reading
Reading at Blackfield
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we want every child to learn and love to read.
Reading is at the heart of our curriculum. We provide children with an ambitious range of rich, high-quality texts that develop their vocabulary, knowledge and understanding of the world. Through reading, discussion and carefully planned teaching, children develop the fluency and comprehension skills they need to become confident, independent readers.
We want children to read widely and often, both to learn and for pleasure. As children progress through the school, they learn to think deeply about texts, make connections, explore different viewpoints and confidently discuss and explain what they have read.
Our Reading Curriculum
Our Reading curriculum sets out how children's knowledge, skills and understanding develop as they progress through Blackfield.
Reading – Intent, Implementation & Impact
Reading – Knowledge & Skills Progression
Phonics & Early Reading
Learning to read begins with securing strong phonics and decoding skills. We teach early reading through Read Write Inc. Phonics, with additional support provided for children who need help to keep up or catch up.

Wrap Around Care
Planet Kids
We are delighted to work with Planet Kids CIC to provide high-quality before and after-school childcare for families at Blackfield Primary and Nursery School.
Planet Kids has supported families in our local community for over 20 years and provides a welcoming and enjoyable environment where children can relax, play and take part in a range of activities.
The provision operates on our school site and is available for children from the age of 3, helping us provide families with convenient childcare from Nursery right through to Year 6.
Breakfast Club
From 7:30am £7 per session
Children can enjoy breakfast and activities before being taken safely into school ready for the start of the day.
After-School Club
From the end of the school day until 6:00pm £18 per session
Children are collected at the end of their school or Nursery day and can enjoy a range of games, activities and opportunities to relax.
Sibling and Early Bird discounts are available.
Holiday Childcare
Planet Kids also offers holiday childcare at Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, helping families with childcare beyond the school term.
Holiday provision is available subject to a minimum number of bookings. Families should contact Planet Kids for upcoming dates, availability and prices.
Booking & Contact
Bookings and enquiries are managed directly by Planet Kids.
Manager: Cass Callen Club Mobile: 07736 918250 Ofsted Registration: 2588980
We are delighted to work with Planet Kids CIC, a well-established and trusted wrap-around childcare provider that has been supporting families in our community for over 20 years. pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - French
pageCache.text:
French
French at Blackfield
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we want children to develop a love of language learning and curiosity about the wider world.
Through learning French, children develop the confidence to listen, speak, read and write in another language. They learn key vocabulary, grammatical structures and French phonology, gradually building their ability to understand and communicate with increasing independence.
Our curriculum encourages children to recognise patterns and make connections between French and English, while developing strategies that will support them in learning languages in the future.
Learning French is also an opportunity to explore French and French-speaking cultures. We want children to recognise similarities and differences between cultures, broaden their understanding of the world and see themselves as respectful global citizens.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Harry Potter Reading Bus
pageCache.text:
Harry Potter Reading Bus
At Blackfield, we want children to develop a genuine love of reading and to experience books as something exciting, enjoyable and magical. Our very own Harry Potter Reading Bus is one of the most unique spaces in our school.
The double-decker bus has been transformed into a dedicated reading environment, filled with books, comfortable reading spaces and Harry Potter-themed features. Children can use the bus at break and lunchtimes to enjoy a book, while classes can also visit to share stories and enjoy reading together.
Created by our children
What makes the Reading Bus particularly special is the story behind it.
The idea was championed by our Pupil Leadership Team and School Council, who worked alongside our PTA, the Friends of Blackfield, to raise the funds needed to make their idea a reality.
It is a fantastic example of pupil voice in action – our children had an ambitious idea for improving their school, helped make it happen and created something that continues to be enjoyed by children across Blackfield.
Making Reading Irresistible
Our Reading Bus reflects our wider ambition to make reading an important and enjoyable part of children's lives. Whether children are discovering a new author, sharing a story with friends or simply finding somewhere quiet to lose themselves in a book, we want them to experience the pleasure that reading can bring.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Music at Blackfield
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we want every child to develop a lifelong love of music and to see themselves as musicians.
Our Music curriculum enables children to explore, create and perform through singing, listening, composing and playing a range of instruments. From their earliest experiences in Nursery, children develop their understanding of sound, rhythm, pulse and pitch before progressively building greater musical knowledge, technical skill, control and confidence.
Children experience a wide range of musical styles, genres and cultures, learning about how music has developed throughout history and the important role it plays in different cultures and communities. They learn to listen carefully, respond to music and use increasingly sophisticated musical vocabulary to express their ideas.
Performance and composition are important parts of Music at Blackfield. Children have opportunities to learn different instruments and to create and perform music both individually and collaboratively, developing their confidence, creativity and self-expression.
Above all, we want children to enjoy making and experiencing music, recognising the positive role it can play in their wellbeing and developing a love of music that extends beyond their time at Blackfield.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Parent Information
pageCache.text:
Parent Information
We want to make it as easy as possible for families to find the information they need.
Below you will find key information about everyday life at Blackfield, including how we communicate with families, term dates, the school day, school meals, uniform and payments.
If you cannot find what you are looking for, please contact the school office and our team will be happy to help.
Communication
We believe that strong communication between home and school is an important part of supporting children successfully.
We email parents through Arbor and use ClassDojo as our main communication platform for sharing school and class information with families. Important whole-school information is also communicated directly to parents when required.
If you need to discuss your child's learning, wellbeing or anything happening in school, their class teacher should usually be your first point of contact, which you can do by email the school office. Our school office team can also help direct your enquiry to the right member of staff.
Arbor Class Dojo Contact Us
Term Dates
Our school term dates are published in advance to help families plan for the academic year.
Blackfield Primary and Nursery School is part of the Inspire Learning Partnership and our term dates may differ from those of other Hampshire schools.
You can also find statutory assessment dates, including KS2 SATs, the Phonics Screening Check and the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check, on our Term Dates page.
The School Day
The school day begins at 8:35am for all pupils. Our Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 playground gates open from 8:25am, allowing children to arrive and be ready for the start of the school day.
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2
Total school hours per week:- Reception, Year 1 and Year 2: 32 hours 55 minutes- Years 3–6: 34 hours 10 minutes
Vehicle Access
For the safety of our children and families, there is a no-drive period on the school grounds at the beginning and end of the school day:
Morning: 8:15am – 8:45am
Afternoon: 3:00pm – 3:35pm
School Meals
Children can enjoy a freshly prepared schools meals, which are cooked on site by our own catering team each day, or bring a packed lunch from home.
Our school kitchen provides a varied menu, with children able to choose from the options available each day. Information about dietary requirements and allergies should be shared with the school so that appropriate arrangements can be discussed.
Week 1 Lunch Menu →Week 2 Lunch Menu →Week 3 Lunch Menu →Free School Meals Information →
Uniform
We expect all children to wear our school uniform. Our uniform is simple, practical and helps children feel proud to belong to the Blackfield community.
Children should wear their school uniform each day, except on their designated PE days when they should come to school wearing their PE kit for the whole day.
Branded Blackfield uniform can be purchased from Skoolkit in Totton or online. Families do not need to purchase every item with a school logo; our full Uniform Policy explains the required uniform and the options available.
We recognise that replacing uniform can be an additional expense for families. If you need support with school uniform, please contact the school office — we will always be happy to help.
Order Uniform from Skoolkit →View our Uniform Policy →
Payments
The easiest way to pay for school dinners, clubs & trips is online through the Arbor Parent Portal. You can sign in here or by downloading the Arbor Parent Portal App.
Please contact the school office on 02380 893132 or at info.bps@ilpartnership.org if you require an Arbor login.
Friends of Blackfield – Our PTA
Friends of Blackfield Primary School (FOBS) is our Parent Teacher Association. FOBS works closely with the school to organise fun events for our children and families, while raising additional funds to support the school.
From Freeze Pop Fridays and second-hand uniform sales to larger events throughout the year, FOBS is a great way to get involved in our school community.
Parents and carers can keep up to date with upcoming events and activities by joining the FOBS Facebook page.
If you have an idea, would like to help at an event, or are interested in getting involved, please contact:
Alex Herring – FOBS Chair fob@ilpartnership.org
Need some help?
If you have a question or cannot find the information you need, please contact our school office.
Telephone: 02380 893132 Email: info.bps@ilpartnership.org
Our team will be happy to help or direct your enquiry to the appropriate member of staff.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Attendance
pageCache.text:
Attendance
Regular attendance is an important part of helping children to feel settled, build strong relationships and make the most of their education. At Blackfield Primary School, we want every child to attend school regularly and arrive on time.
We recognise that there can sometimes be genuine barriers to attendance. Where attendance becomes a concern, we will work with children and families to understand what is making attendance difficult and offer appropriate support.
Reporting an Absence
If your child is unable to attend school, please contact the school office as early as possible on each day of absence on 02380 893132, giving the reason for their absence.
If we have not received a reason for a child's absence, the school will contact parents/carers as part of our safeguarding and attendance procedures.
Where possible, medical and dental appointments should be arranged outside of the school day. If this is not possible, please provide the school with details of the appointment.
Punctuality
The school day begins at 8:35am.
Our playground gates open from 8:25am, allowing children to arrive and be ready for the start of learning.
Children arriving after 8:35am will be recorded as late. Persistent lateness can have a significant impact on a child's education and we will work with families where punctuality becomes a concern.
Supporting Good Attendance
We know that difficulties with attendance can have many different causes. Our approach is to identify concerns early and work in partnership with families to help children attend school successfully.
This may include support from school staff and, where appropriate, working with external services or the Local Authority.
Parents and carers are encouraged to contact us as early as possible if there are circumstances affecting their child's attendance. The sooner we understand the difficulty, the sooner we can work together to help.
Leave of Absence During Term Time
Parents and carers should avoid taking children out of school during term time.
Schools may only grant a leave of absence in exceptional circumstances, and each request is considered individually. Requests should be made in advance using the school's Leave of Absence Request Form.
Unauthorised absence may result in the Local Authority considering a penalty notice or other legal intervention in accordance with the national framework for school attendance.
Request for Leave of Absence Form →
Information about Penalty Notices →
When Your Child Is Struggling to Attend
Sometimes a child may find attending school difficult because of anxiety, emotional wellbeing or other circumstances.
Please speak to us rather than struggling alone. We will work with you and your child to understand the barriers to attendance and agree appropriate support.
Contact the school Inclusion & Family Liaison Lead

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Communication
pageCache.text:
Communication
Good communication between home and school is an important part of supporting our children. We aim to make it simple for parents and carers to know where to find information and who to contact when they need us.
Arbor
Arbor is our main communication and information system for parents.
Parents and carers use Arbor to receive school emails and important information, update contact details and consents, book parents’ evenings and access information about their child.
It is important that all parents and carers have access to Arbor and keep their contact details up to date.
ClassDojo
We use ClassDojo to share classroom news, photographs, reminders and updates about children's learning.
Nursery and Year R ClassDojo is used for two-way communication between families and the Early Years team.
Years 1–6 ClassDojo is used by the school to share updates with families. Messaging is not used for parents to contact teachers.
For questions or messages in Years 1–6, please contact the school office, who will make sure your message reaches the appropriate member of staff.
Contacting Us
Our school office is the first point of contact for general enquiries, appointments, absence reporting or if you are unsure who you need to speak to.
Telephone: 02380 893132 Email: info.bps@ilpartnership.org Office hours: 8:00am–4:00pm, Monday to Friday
If you need to speak to your child's teacher, the office team can pass on a message or arrange for the appropriate member of staff to contact you.
Keeping Up to Date
Important information and whole-school communications are sent through Arbor. We also celebrate school life and share news through our website and social media channels.
Facebook → Instagram →
We value face-to-face communication too. Members of our leadership team are regularly on the school gates at the beginning and end of the day and are always happy to say hello.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackfield Primary and Nursery School - Ofsted
pageCache.text:
Ofsted
Blackfield Primary and Nursery School is proud to be a GOOD school.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection took place on 21st September 2022.
What Ofsted Said About Blackfield
A happy, welcoming school
“Blackfield is a welcoming and happy school where staff and pupils take pride in their community.”
Inspectors highlighted that our INSPIRE values run through every aspect of school life, with pupils demonstrating positive attitudes and high expectations.
Strong relationships where children feel safe
“Pupils feel safe because they know that adults listen to them and care about them.”
Ofsted recognised the strong relationships between staff and pupils, describing children as kind and considerate and highlighting the particularly strong relationships established within Early Years.
A wide, rich education beyond the classroom
Ofsted recognised the breadth of opportunities available to our children, highlighting our trips and exciting curriculum experiences, wide range of clubs, pupil leadership opportunities and even our school radio station. Inspectors found that these opportunities enable pupils to develop their individual talents and interests.

You can also find statutory assessment dates, including KS2 SATs, the Phonics Screening Check and the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check, on our Term Dates page.
The School Day
The school day begins at 8:35am for all pupils. Our Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 playground gates open from 8:25am, allowing children to arrive and be ready for the start of the school day.
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2
Total school hours per week:- Reception, Year 1 and Year 2: 32 hours 55 minutes- Years 3–6: 34 hours 10 minutes
Vehicle Access
For the safety of our children and families, there is a no-drive period on the school grounds at the beginning and end of the school day:
Morning: 8:15am – 8:45am
Afternoon: 3:00pm – 3:35pm
School Meals
Children can enjoy a freshly prepared schools meals, which are cooked on site by our own catering team each day, or bring a packed lunch from home.
Our school kitchen provides a varied menu, with children able to choose from the options available each day. Information about dietary requirements and allergies should be shared with the school so that appropriate arrangements can be discussed.
Week 1 Lunch Menu →Week 2 Lunch Menu →Week 3 Lunch Menu →Free School Meals Information →
Uniform
We expect all children to wear our school uniform. Our uniform is simple, practical and helps children feel proud to belong to the Blackfield community.
Children should wear their school uniform each day, except on their designated PE days when they should come to school wearing their PE kit for the whole day.
Branded Blackfield uniform can be purchased from Skoolkit in Totton or online. Families do not need to purchase every item with a school logo; our full Uniform Policy explains the required uniform and the options available.
We recognise that replacing uniform can be an additional expense for families. If you need support with school uniform, please contact the school office — we will always be happy to help.
Order Uniform from Skoolkit →View our Uniform Policy →
Payments
The easiest way to pay for school dinners, clubs & trips is online through the Arbor Parent Portal. You can sign in here or by downloading the Arbor Parent Portal App.
Please contact the school office on 02380 893132 or at info.bps@ilpartnership.org if you require an Arbor login.
Friends of Blackfield – Our PTA
Friends of Blackfield Primary School (FOBS) is our Parent Teacher Association. FOBS works closely with the school to organise fun events for our children and families, while raising additional funds to support the school.
From Freeze Pop Fridays and second-hand uniform sales to larger events throughout the year, FOBS is a great way to get involved in our school community.
Parents and carers can keep up to date with upcoming events and activities by joining the FOBS Facebook page.
If you have an idea, would like to help at an event, or are interested in getting involved, please contact:
Alex Herring – FOBS Chair fob@ilpartnership.org
Need some help?
If you have a question or cannot find the information you need, please contact our school office.
Telephone: 02380 893132 Email: info.bps@ilpartnership.org
Our team will be happy to help or direct your enquiry to the appropriate member of staff.

Phonics & Early Reading
Learning to Read at Blackfield
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we believe that learning to read confidently and fluently is one of the most important foundations for children's future success.
We teach early reading through Read Write Inc. Phonics, a systematic synthetic phonics programme. Children are taught to recognise sounds, blend them together to read words and develop increasing accuracy, fluency and confidence as readers.
Children's progress is assessed regularly so that teaching can be closely matched to their stage of reading development. Children who need additional support receive extra practice and targeted intervention to help them keep up and catch up.
Read Write Inc. Phonics
We follow the Read Write Inc. Phonics programme to provide a consistent and carefully sequenced approach to the teaching of early reading.
Through the programme, children:
Teaching begins in Reception and continues through Key Stage 1. Children in Key Stage 2 who have not yet secured the necessary phonics knowledge continue to receive appropriate phonics teaching and support.
RWI Phonics: A Guide for Parents
develop fluency and expression through repeated reading;
develop their understanding of what they read;
practise spelling and writing alongside their reading.
Keeping Up and Catching Up
We want every child to become a successful reader.
Children's phonics knowledge and reading progress are assessed regularly. This allows us to quickly identify children who are at risk of falling behind and provide additional teaching and practice.
Our aim is for children to keep up rather than need to catch up, while providing intensive and carefully targeted support where this is required.
Supporting Reading at Home
Parents and carers play an important part in helping children become confident readers.
Children take home reading material that supports the phonics knowledge they are developing in school. We encourage families to read regularly with their children and to enjoy sharing a wide range of books and stories together.

Science
Science at Blackfield
At Blackfield Primary and Nursery School, we want children to develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about the world around them.
Our Science curriculum develops children's scientific knowledge alongside the skills needed to work and think like scientists. Children are encouraged to observe, investigate, question, explain and use evidence to develop their understanding of scientific ideas.
Through practical investigations and different types of scientific enquiry, children learn to make predictions, identify patterns, carry out fair and comparative tests, classify and group, observe changes over time and use secondary sources to answer questions. As they progress through the school, children develop increasingly precise scientific vocabulary and learn to use it confidently when explaining their thinking.
We also want children to understand the importance of Science beyond the classroom: how it has changed our lives, its importance to our future and the role that science can play in understanding and protecting our planet.

Our Curriculum
Our curriculum is built around three key aims: for children to master key knowledge and skills, develop effective learning behaviours and characteristics, and develop a strong moral compass. We want children to know more and remember more, while becoming curious, resilient, independent and thoughtful learners.
Much of our curriculum is brought together through Integrated Learning Units (ILUs), which make meaningful connections between subjects and give learning a clear purpose. Other subjects, including Mathematics, PE, Music, RE and French, are taught discretely where this enables greater depth and progression.
